_:
cvk is a small Obsidian plugin that drives Obsidian Canvas entirely from the keyboard. The repo is ~/i/cvk. cd to ~/i/cvk before doing anything: the plan tool only resolves plan/cvk.plan.json relative to cwd.

STACK. Plain TypeScript. esbuild bundles main.ts to main.js (format cjs, platform browser, 'obsidian' external). vitest for tests. pnpm only, never npm and never npx. No svelte, no framework, no runtime dependencies at all.

LAYOUT (everything at the repo root, there is no src/ folder):
  canvas_ops.ts     pure geometry and ordering. Imports nothing. Every function in it is unit tested.
  canvas_bridge.ts  takes a live canvas object typed `canvas: any` and mutates it. Imports only ./canvas_ops. It must NEVER import 'obsidian', which is what makes it unit testable against a fake canvas.
  main.ts           the Obsidian Plugin subclass. Wiring only: it registers commands that look up the active canvas and call canvas_bridge.
  settings.ts       the settings tab. Must NEVER import ./main (that would be a cycle).
  tests/            vitest tests plus the tests/fake_canvas.ts helper.

CODE STYLE, repo wide, non negotiable:
  snake_case for every variable and every function. Tabs for indentation. Single quotes. Semicolons.
  NO COMMENTS ANYWHERE in any file you write. Names and structure carry the meaning.
  All user facing text (command names, setting names, setting descriptions) in lowercase.
  No variables that are used only once.

OBSIDIAN CANVAS FACTS. These were read out of Obsidian 1.13.4's app.js. The canvas API is undocumented but every line below is verified correct. Do not second guess it and do not look for a public API, there is none.
  The canvas view's type string is 'canvas'. The live canvas object hangs off the view as view.canvas.
  canvas.nodes is a Map<string, node>. canvas.edges is a Map<string, edge>. canvas.selection is a Set that holds BOTH nodes and edges, so nodes are filtered out of it with `canvas.nodes.get(x.id) === x`.
  A node has .id .x .y .width .height .color and the methods .moveTo({x,y}) .resize({width,height}) .setColor(color, render) .isEditable() .startEditing() .getBBox() which returns {minX,minY,maxX,maxY} and .getData() which returns an object with a .type of 'text' | 'file' | 'link' | 'group'.
  canvas.createTextNode({pos:{x,y}, size:{width,height}, save:false}) creates a text card, attaches it, renders it, selects only it, starts editing it, and returns it.
  canvas.createGroupNode({pos:{x,y}, size:{width,height}, save:false, focus:false}) creates a group without stealing focus into its label editor.
  Edges are added with canvas.importData({nodes: [], edges: [...]}, false). Obsidian computes fromSide and toSide itself from the two nodes' positions, so NEVER compute sides. An edge object is {id, fromNode, toNode, fromEnd, toEnd}. toEnd defaults to 'arrow' and fromEnd defaults to 'none', so a two way link is fromEnd:'arrow'. Both node ids must already exist in canvas.nodes.
  Node and edge ids are 16 lowercase hex characters.
  canvas.config.defaultTextNodeDimensions is {width:250, height:60}.
  canvas.requestSave() both persists the file and pushes an undo entry. Call it exactly once per user action.
  Also available: canvas.selectOnly(node), canvas.deselectAll(), canvas.deleteSelection(), canvas.removeNode(node), canvas.panIntoView(bbox), canvas.wrapperEl.focus({preventScroll:true}).
  canvas.readonly is true in a read only canvas and every command must refuse to run then.

OBSIDIAN ALREADY BINDS THESE INSIDE A CANVAS. Do not reimplement them, do not rebind them, do not give any command in this plugin one of these key combinations:
  arrows nudge the selection by one grid cell, shift+arrows nudge by five, mod+a select all, mod+z undo, mod+shift+z and mod+y redo, shift+1 zoom to fit, shift+2 zoom to selection, escape deselect, delete and backspace delete the selection.

WHY EVERY COMMAND CHECKS FOR TYPING. Obsidian's hotkey manager listens on window in the CAPTURE phase, ahead of the editor. A bare key hotkey such as Enter or Tab would therefore fire while the user is typing inside a card. Every command in this plugin refuses to run when an INPUT, a TEXTAREA or a contenteditable element has focus.

TESTS. NEVER write a test, never edit a test, never fix an import inside a test. Every test file already exists under plan/tests/ and each step gives you the exact cp command for it. Copy it byte for byte, do not open it to "check" it, do not adapt an assertion that looks wrong. Make the test pass by changing the implementation. Every gate byte compares the placed tests against plan/tests/, so a single altered byte fails the gate.

COMMANDS: `pnpm test` runs vitest, `pnpm check` runs tsc --noEmit, `pnpm build` bundles and deploys into every Obsidian vault.

After marking each step, run `git add -A` and commit with a long message that names the step id and explains every change.

build_deploy.s:
Build the plugin, deploy it into the vault, and enable it.

Run:

  pnpm build

That bundles main.ts into main.js and then runs deploy.mjs, which copies main.js and manifest.json into ~/54/.obsidian/plugins/cvk/ and writes a .hotreload marker there.

Then enable the plugin. ~/54/.obsidian/community-plugins.json is a JSON array of enabled plugin ids and currently reads:

[
  "hot-reload",
  "obsidian-git"
]

Rewrite it to:

[
  "hot-reload",
  "obsidian-git",
  "cvk"
]

Do not touch any other file under ~/54/.obsidian/. Do not edit ~/54/.obsidian/hotkeys.json — the plugin's own default hotkeys come from the manifest of commands, not from that file, and it holds the user's existing bindings.

You cannot see Obsidian, so do not claim the shortcuts work. The gate proves the built bundle contains the commands and landed in the vault; the user verifies the keys by hand.
build_deploy.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && pnpm check && pnpm build && test -f main.js && test -f "$HOME/54/.obsidian/plugins/cvk/main.js" && test -f "$HOME/54/.obsidian/plugins/cvk/manifest.json" && test -f "$HOME/54/.obsidian/plugins/cvk/.hotreload" && grep -qF '"cvk"' "$HOME/54/.obsidian/community-plugins.json" && grep -qF 'ungroup-selection' main.js && grep -qF 'createTextNode' main.js && grep -qF 'defaultTextNodeDimensions' main.js

readme_repo.s:
Write the README and publish the repo.

Create README.md at the repo root with exactly this content:

# cvk — canvas keys

drive obsidian canvas from the keyboard.

## defaults

| keys | does |
| --- | --- |
| `Alt` + arrow | new connected node that way, arrow pointing at it |
| `Alt+Shift` + arrow | same, but the link points both ways |
| `Mod` + arrow | focus the nearest node that way |
| `Mod+Alt` + arrow | move the selection by the configured step |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | focus next / previous node, top-to-bottom then left-to-right |
| `Enter` | edit the selected node |
| `Mod+Backspace` | delete the selection |
| `Alt+C` / `Alt+Shift+C` | connect the selected nodes into a chain, one-way / two-way |
| `Alt+P` | cycle the selection through the six canvas colours and back to none |
| `Alt+G` / `Alt+Shift+G` | group the selection / remove the selected group |
| unbound | resize node up/down/left/right — bind them in settings then hotkeys |

every one of these is rebindable in settings then hotkeys, and none of them fire while a card is being edited.

`Mod+Alt` + arrow is the one to watch on linux: some window managers grab it for workspace switching. rebind if so.

## already in obsidian, not reimplemented here

arrows nudge by grid, `Shift` + arrows nudge by five, `Mod+A` select all, `Mod+Z` / `Mod+Shift+Z` undo and redo, `Shift+1` zoom to fit, `Shift+2` zoom to selection, `Escape` deselect, `Delete` delete selection.

## settings

| setting | default | does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| move step | 50 | pixels a node moves or resizes per keypress |
| new node gap | 50 | pixels between a node and the node created next to it |

## dev

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev      # watch build
pnpm test     # vitest
pnpm check    # tsc --noEmit
pnpm build    # production bundle + copy into every obsidian vault
```

canvas_ops.ts is pure geometry and imports nothing. canvas_bridge.ts drives a live canvas and never imports obsidian, so both are unit tested without an obsidian runtime. main.ts is registration only.

Then commit everything and publish:

  git add -A
  git commit -m "cvk: keyboard shortcuts for obsidian canvas"
  gh repo create 144126/cvk --public --source=. --remote=origin --push

If the repo already exists, `git push -u origin HEAD` instead.
readme_repo.t: test -f README.md && grep -qF 'new connected node that way' README.md && grep -qF 'move step' README.md && gh repo view 144126/cvk >/dev/null 2>&1 && git log --oneline -1 >/dev/null
